patient.chief_complaint: Five-day rapidly progressive ascending leg weakness and areflexia with bilateral facial diplegia, preceded by Campylobacter gastroenteritis 2 weeks ago. Unable to walk. Respiratory function declining.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. W. is a 35-year-old physical therapist presenting with a 5-day history of rapidly progressive neurological symptoms. Two weeks before admission, he had confirmed Campylobacter jejuni gastroenteritis (stool culture positive at an urgent care clinic) lasting 4 days. He recovered but 10 days later developed bilateral foot tingling. Over the following 5 days, weakness ascended rapidly from his feet to his hips. He is now unable to walk. Yesterday he noticed bilateral facial drooping and slurred speech. He has had dysphagia for thin liquids since this morning. As a physical therapist, he recognized the pattern immediately and came to the ED. FVC on arrival is 1.8 L (43% predicted). He is alarmed and asking for IVIG. He has no bowel or bladder symptoms. No neck stiffness. No fever since his gastroenteritis resolved.

cardiac_monitoring.rhythm_summary: Sinus rhythm with sustained sinus tachycardia, mean rate 118 bpm
findings: Baseline rhythm on the admission ECG: Sinus tachycardia at 118 bpm, QTc 468 ms
Persistent sinus tachycardia, rate 118 bpm at rest, sustained on the recording — the commonest autonomic manifestation in this disease and, on its own, not an indication for intervention
QTc 468 ms carried over from the admission ECG and unchanged on the recording — relevant to the choice of any QT-prolonging drug during the admission
No bradyarrhythmia, no pause beyond 2 seconds, no AV block and no sustained tachyarrhythmia over the monitored period
cardiac_monitoring.impression: Continuous inpatient telemetry through the period of maximal weakness. Autonomic involvement affects about two thirds of patients with Guillain-Barré syndrome and is a leading cause of in-hospital death, so this recording is a monitoring requirement rather than a diagnostic test: what it looks for is the bradyarrhythmia, the pause beyond 3 seconds and the blood-pressure lability that trigger ICU escalation, alongside serial respiratory function. Sustained sinus tachycardia is documented. It is the mildest and most frequent autonomic sign here, requires no treatment in itself, and is monitored because it often precedes the bradyarrhythmias that do. Beyond the rate, the recording is normal. That is the expected result in this patient and it is not a wasted test: the value of monitoring in this disease lies in what it excludes during the window in which dysautonomia can appear. The patient is in critical care, which is where this monitoring belongs: airway interventions provoke vagal responses, and the recording is read alongside serial respiratory function rather than in isolation.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe AIDP requiring mechanical ventilation (post-Campylobacter)

differential.key_features: Anti-GM1 positive; pure motor; reduced CMAPs; share Campylobacter antecedent — repeat EMG distinguishes.
Descending pattern with no sensory involvement.
Skin / scalp exam; no exposure history.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, CMP, HIV, anti-GM1/anti-GQ1b ganglioside antibodies, and stool culture / Campylobacter serology if recent diarrhea
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild leukocytosis / elevated inflammatory markers reflecting antecedent infection; ganglioside antibodies for variant typing; trigger identification (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, Mycoplasma, HIV)

optimal_actions.action: Order nerve conduction studies and needle EMG (EMG/NCS)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Demyelinating pattern (prolonged DML, conduction block, reduced CV, absent F-waves) consistent with AIDP, or reduced CMAP amplitudes in axonal variants (AMAN/AMSAN)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation — elevated protein with cell count <10/μL; may be normal in the first week of illness

optimal_actions.action: Order bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) and repeat every 4–6 hours
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline and serial FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF; deterioration to FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted triggers ICU transfer / intubation

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for IVIG vs plasma exchange evidence to guide disease-modifying therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) and plasma exchange are equivalently effective first-line therapies; combination not superior

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions / contraindications for IVIG (renal function, IgA deficiency screen) and/or plasma exchange (coagulation, calcium, hemodynamics)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that IVIG can be given safely (no severe renal impairment, no IgA deficiency) or that plasma exchange is appropriate (adequate vascular access, stable coagulation)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus tachycardia or bradycardia; conduction or repolarisation abnormalities reflecting autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Start continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry for the period of maximal weakness and keep it running alongside serial respiratory function. Autonomic instability affects about two thirds of patients and is a leading cause of in-hospital death: bradyarrhythmias, pauses beyond 3 seconds and blood-pressure lability are what trigger ICU escalation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sustained sinus tachycardia at 118 bpm with no bradyarrhythmia, no pause beyond 2 seconds and no AV block: the mildest autonomic manifestation, and a recording whose value is in excluding the arrhythmias that would escalate care

useless_tools.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

critical_actions: Intubate and mechanically ventilate; ICU admission.
contraindicated_actions: Do not give corticosteroids as monotherapy.
Do not use neuromuscular blockade outside intubation context.
key_reasoning_points: Severe AIDP with respiratory failure mandates ICU and ventilation.
Post-Campylobacter cases warrant repeat EMG for AIDP-vs-AMAN clarification at 1–2 weeks.
Autonomic instability is a leading cause of mortality in severe GBS — continuous monitoring is mandatory.
